conviction_note: The findings sum to +3.0 and the scaled number is +1.44 (abs_move 12, p_up 56). The two numbers have the same sign. Every positive is an inference from company documents: Q2's one-offs, the Q2->Q3 seasonal step-up, the Pax ramp and the guide arithmetic. None of it is a hidden Q3 number. Upside skew and a short that built 15% into the print raise the size of a beat reaction, not the odds of a beat. That is why p_up sits only 6 points above 50.
bar: The Q3 2026 revenue consensus is about $182.4-183.3m. Earnings Whispers via search snippet: $183.32m and EPS -$0.21 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/nvcr). Benzinga: about $182.4m and EPS -$0.23/-$0.24 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVCR/earnings). The two sources agree within 0.5%. The company guide is FY26 revenue $710-725m, raised on 2026-07-23 from $690-710m, and adj. EBITDA $0-15m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm). H1 revenue is $357.7m, so the guide implies $176-184m a quarter in H2. Consensus sits at the top of that range. Note: the sweep row's 'FY26 revenue guide $675-705m' is stale.
positioning_check: MarketBeat, record date 2026-10-15 (FINRA published 2026-10-26): 12,823,054 shares short, 11.78% of float, 7.7 days to cover. That is up from 11,163,094 shares (10.3%, 10.05 DTC) at 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/NVCR/short-interest/). The short is crowded-ish and building into the print. Baseline skew is -27.98 vol points (25d put IV below 25d call IV), so the market is paying for upside. Caveat: the ATM spread is 59% of mid and total OI is only 2,360, so the option signal is indicative. Spot is $14.42: -9.6% over 20 days, -7.5% over 5 days, 28% below the 52-week high, and back near the $14.51 close after the June TRIDENT failure. The last two prints moved +27.5% and +28.4%.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue should land at about $185-188m, roughly 1-3% above the $182.4-183.3m consensus. Q2's $183.6m included $2.8m of one-time revenue (German approval rates and age claims, US deductible, France), so the underlying Q2 run rate is about $180.8m. Q3 has stepped up sequentially in both prior years: +3.1% in 2024 ($150.4m to $155.1m) and +5.3% in 2025 ($158.8m to $167.2m, including $3.3m of FX). Gio active patients were +11% YoY at 4,636. Optune Pax ended Q2 with 285 actives from 418 prescriptions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue of $183.6m beat the $172.4m consensus by 6.5% with a guide raise, and the stock rose 28.4%. Q1 2026: +27.5%. Q3 2025: $167.2m, stock -4.9%. July 2025: -24.1%. This name has paid for revenue beats lately.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $183m equals reported Q2 revenue. The Street has therefore modelled a flat quarter on a base that held $2.8m of one-offs, and has assumed no seasonal step-up and no Pax ramp. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would not have fallen 9.6% in 20 days back to post-TRIDENT levels while shorts added 1.66m shares.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 seasonal step-up comes from a separate document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645113/000164511325000043/nvcr-20250930xpr1111.htm). The one-time items come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15276766716830720). The second finding rests on the same Q3 revenue level.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide arithmetic points to a raise. FY $710-725m less H1 $357.7m leaves H2 at $352-367m, or $176-184m a quarter. Management said the high end is 'basically in line with the Q2 results'. A Q3 at or above about $183m leaves Q4 needing only about $169-184m, so at least the low end would likely be lifted. That would be the third raise of the year, after February's initial guide, the April raise and the July raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was raised at both Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 (the July raise was from $690-710m to $710-725m), and the stock rose 27-28% each time. Q3 2025, with no raise, fell 4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The $183m Q3 consensus already implies the top of the range, so only a raise above $725m adds information. A stock pricing that in would not be sitting near its June low with short interest rising.
findings.independence: Shares the Q3 revenue basis with the first finding, so the two are not independent. This one is sized smaller on that account. Guide figures from the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm.

findings.finding: The Optune Pax (pancreatic) launch is running ahead of the company's own expectations. Q1 brought 169 prescriptions and 83 actives. Q2 brought 418 prescriptions and 285 actives. At the 9 Sep Wells Fargo conference management said about 70% of prescriptions convert to active patients and private payer coverage is ahead of schedule. Japan's MHLW approved Pax on 1 Oct, so Q3 Pax actives and revenue (Q2 revenue was $1.6m) are the growth metric the release will report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print (first Pax data) rose 27.5% and the Q2 print (Pax 285 actives) rose 28.4%. The Q2 call flagged repeat prescribing as the Q3 priority and half of prescribers as one-time writers, so a stall would be punished.
findings.why_not_priced: The conference comments came after the July print, and the stock has fallen about 20% since early September ($17.94 on Sep 4 to $14.42). A market already pricing a continued Pax ramp would not have given back most of the Q2 reaction.
findings.independence: Q2 Pax figures come from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm). The Japan approval comes from the 8-K of 2026-10-01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645113/000164511326000071/paxjapandecisionpr.htm). This finding is net of the rest of the company: Pax is under 2% of revenue in dollars and matters for the multiple, while Gio (+11% actives) carries the revenue line.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 15% into the print, from 11.16m shares at 2026-09-30 to 12.82m at 2026-10-15 (11.8% of float, 7.7 days to cover). Over the same period the 25d skew is -28 vol points, so upside calls are bid, and the stock sits -9.6% over 20 days near its post-TRIDENT low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints moved +27.5% and +28.4% on event-day volume 7-8x the 20-day median, which is consistent with short covering amplifying beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism here, not a direction. It raises the payoff of a beat more than it changes the odds of one. The option skew already prices upside, so only the asymmetry beyond that is counted.
findings.independence: The option skew comes from a different source (the sealed baseline, Yahoo chain) and points the same way.

findings.finding: Q2's adjusted EBITDA of $10.8m included a $4.9m tariff refund in cost of revenue and $2.8m of one-time revenue, and management guided gross margin to 'mid-70s' for the rest of 2026 against Q2's 78%. Q3 EBITDA and EPS will therefore step down sequentially on optics, though EPS consensus of -$0.21 to -$0.24 against Q2's -$0.13 already reflects this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows no case of this name trading on margin alone. Its prints have turned on revenue and the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the EPS consensus has already normalised. What remains is headline risk if adjusted EBITDA prints near zero.
findings.independence: The tariff refund and one-time revenue are confirmed in the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm).

findings.finding: An Item 8.01 8-K reported a cybersecurity incident discovered in mid-August 2026. It exposed internal patient IDs for more than 1,400 US records, plus identifying data for fewer than 50 patients and contact details for providers and employees. The company stated no device access, no operational impact and no expected material effect, and it may record response costs in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since Sep 1 and the company calls it immaterial. Only the cost line or any notification commentary in the release is new.

findings.finding: FX is a small sequential headwind. Monthly EUR/USD averages run about 1.16 in Q2 and about 1.15 in Q3 (rounded), roughly -1% on about $45m of euro revenue, or about $0.3-0.5m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 revenue carried a $3.3m FX benefit and the stock fell 4.9%. FX has not driven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro proxy, and the effect is too small for the Street to adjust for.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The company has not confirmed the transmission.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-28 Novocure announced a clinical trial collaboration and supply agreement with Verastem to test TTFields with VS-7375, an oral KRAS G12D inhibitor, in pancreatic cancer. This positions Pax alongside rather than against the KRAS class that the Wells Fargo summary named as competition.
findings.why_not_priced: It was announced on the day of the seal, so it is partly priced today. It is pipeline news with no quarter impact.

outside_window.finding: The FDA decision on the PMA for TTFields in brain metastases from NSCLC (Optune Maia) is 'on track for a Q4 2026 decision' (Q2 release and call, and the Wells Fargo conference on 9 Sep). It could only enter the window if the release discloses an approval, which nothing indicates. If approved it is a material positive for the multiple.
Completion of enrollment in the Phase 3 KEYNOTE D58 trial (newly diagnosed GBM) is expected in Q4 2026.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A tariff refund repeating in Q3 cost of revenue
rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into the margin/EBITDA finding. Q2 booked $4.9m and nothing sources a Q3 repeat.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the skew (upside paid) and cuts against the 20-day run-up (-9.6%). A beat would land on a short that is building. The risk is that this is the third straight 'beat and raise' setup and the Street may already model it.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (documents beat inference): the Q3 revenue finding is an inference from Q2 documents and seasonality, not a Q3 number, so it goes from +1.5 to +1.2.
Rule 3 / 'two readings of one document': the guidance-raise finding rests on the same Q3 revenue level as finding 1, so it goes from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 7 and rule 5 ('positioning ... do not file'): short interest is a mechanism that amplifies, not a direction, so it goes from +1.0 to +0.5.
Rule 1 (reaction veto): checked. This name bought its last two beats at +27-28%, so the veto does not shrink the revenue findings further; p_up goes from 57 to 56 for inference-only evidence.
Rule 6 (bar and window): the bar is confirmed from two agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, the stale sweep guide is flagged, and the brain-mets FDA decision stays in outside_window.
Rules 2, 4, 8 and 9: the cyber incident is filed as a one_off at a fraction; no financing; Pax is sized net of Gio. No other change.
